text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Sheffield United and West Ham at Bramall Lane.
It has been a dismal first season back in the top-flight for the hosts, picking up just two victories so far this term to leave them eight points from safety.

This is the Blades' first Premier League game of 2024 after a potentially confidence-boosting 4-0 away win at League Two side Gillingham last weekend, and with both of their league victories this season coming at Bramall Lane, the home fans will be hoping for another much-needed win here.
Unlike their hosts, West Ham suffered FA Cup disappointment last time out, losing 1-0 away at second-tier Bristol City.
The Hammers are still in good Premier League nick, however, currently sixth ahead of the likes of Manchester United and Chelsea.
A run of four league games without defeat has helped, with three victories during that spell, and another three points here could close the gap on fifth-placed rivals Tottenham to just three points.
Chris Wilder hands new signing Brereton a Premier League debut in attack as one of four changes from his team's last Premier League outing, a 2-0 defeat at Manchester City.
The Chile international comes in for Anis Ben Slimane and will join Osula, who scored a brace at Gillingham, in attack.

McAtee also netted a double against the Gills, enough to earn him a spot in midfield in place of Norwood, while Hamer comes in for Luke Thomas, who had his loan from Leicester City terminated last week.
Ahmedhodzic for George Baldock is the other change.
David Moyes also goes with four changes from his team's last league game, a goalless draw at home to Brighton in early January.

With Mohammed Kudus at the Africa Cup of Nations and Michail Antonio injured, Cornet and Ings are handed rare starts, with the former having made just one substitute appearance in the Premier League this term.
Coufal and Zouma also come into the starting XI with Johnson and Ogbonna dropping to the bench, while Edson Alvarez is absent altogether.
The two teams make their way onto the Bramall Lane pitch ahead of a big game at both ends of the table.
Who can take the three points? We will find out shortly!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way in Sheffield!
Robinson heaves an early long throw into the Hammers' box, though the returning Zouma makes an important header before his fellow defenders finish the job by clearing upfield.
West Ham have won each of their last eight Premier League games against newly promoted sides, since a 1-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest in August 2022.
Both sides have held each other at arm's length so far, with the two defences looking largely untroubled.
Sheffield United have scored six goals fewer than any other Premier League side so far this term, while only Manchester United have scored less goals than West Ham in the top half.
Hamer tries his luck from range, and while he is certainly capable of finding the back of the net from that distance, this time he fires well wide.
The Blades have shaded these opening exchanges.
Vinicius sends a rasping drive goalwards from 30 yards out, but it only serves to sting the palms of Areola, who gathers at the second attempt.
The home fans must surely be encouraged by their team's start, however.
There's a nervy moment for Foderingham as he comes for a long throw and doesn't get there, but Ings' effort bounces well wide of the target, much to the majority of Bramall Lane's relief.
CHANCE! A loose touch in the hosts' defence is latched upon by the opportunistic Ings, who lays it into Bowen.
He makes the space for a shot on his left foot, but he drags well wide of the target.
Bowen has been on fire on the road this season, and he will be disappointed not to have made Foderingham work there.
Zouma brings down Osula right on the edge of the box, and the home side will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
Hamer has grabbed the ball and will almost certainly be the man trusted to take it.
It is a wasted opportunity in the end, as Hamer can only hit the wall with his free-kick, with Emerson nodding away from danger.
West Ham fail to fully clear another long throw, and the ball sits up nicely for Brooks.
It's a wild effort from Brooks, though, and the ball soars high into the stands.
Twenty minutes on the clock at Bramall Lane, and while the hosts have been the better team, it's the visitors who have had the best opportunity when Bowen fired wide.
Wilder will be desperate for his side to make the most of being on top.
Wilder has won just one of his five meetings with West Ham in all competitions (one draw, three defeats), winning 1-0 with the Blades at Bramall Lane in the Premier League in January 2020.
Space opens up for Brereton to try for a goal on his Premier League debut, though his right-footed effort is straight down the throat of Areola.
Sheffield United lost 1-0 at home to West Ham the last time they hosted them in the league (November 2020) – they have not lost consecutive home league meetings with the Hammers since February 1963.
CHANCE! Trusty finds himself in too much space as a corner comes in, but he can't make full use of the free header as he nods straight at Areola.
That's exactly the type of chance that needs to be put away if the Blades are to haul themselves out of trouble.

GOOOAAALLL!!! CORNET FIRES WEST HAM IN FRONT!!! It's been a hugely frustrating campaign for Cornet, and this will mean the world to him as he repays Moyes' faith with a goal on his first league start of the season.
The ball sits up for Ings in the box, and while his initial shot is blocked, it deflects kindly to the back post for Cornet, who makes no mistake as he fires into the back of the net.
1-0 to the Hammers!
In a game that they have been the better side in, that goal will be another huge blow to the Blades' hopes of survival.
Wilder will be desperate for a response, but as so often has been the case this season, his team's toothlessness in front of goal could make that difficult.
Sheffield United have become the first side to concede 50 Premier League goals this season, doing so in just 21 games.
In the competition's history, only Barnsley in 1997-98 (19) have conceded 50 in fewer games from the start of a campaign.
West Ham have lost just one of their last 13 Premier League games in which they've scored the opening goal (nine wins, three draws), losing to Manchester City in September last year.
That doesn't bode well for the hosts.
Osula receives the ball in the box before turning and firing, though his shot from a tight angle only flies out for a throw-in on the opposite side of the pitch.
The first booking of the game goes to Hamer for a cynical pullback on Fornals, who was on the charge.
Bowen's cutback into the box is cleared, but only to Ings.
The former Southampton man fires goalwards, but Trusty is well-placed to make a vital block to ensure his team don't fall two goals behind.
Ward-Prowse goes in the book for bringing down Bogle in midfield after Cornet gave the ball away.
GOOOAAALLL!!! BRERETON SCORES ON HIS PREMIER LEAGUE DEBUT!!! What a huge moment this could be for Sheffield United as their new forward finds the back of the net to level.
Trusty nods a long ball into the box, and though Osula's initial header is saved brilliantly by Areola, the ball falls kindly for Brereton to rifle home and make it 1-1!
We are into two minutes of additional time as the hosts look to take advantage of their newfound momentum and score a quick second before the break.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 1-1 WEST HAM

The half-time whistle blows, probably coming at a bad time for Sheffield United as they go into the break level at 1-1 with West Ham thanks to Brereton's 44th-minute leveller, his first goal for his new team.

The Blades shaded the opening exchanges, but it was the visitors who took the lead with 28 minutes gone, Cornet pouncing upon a loose ball to fire home on his first Premier League start of the season.

It appeared Moyes' men would take that advantage into the interval, but after Osula saw a header saved by Areola, Brereton latched onto the rebound to power home and give his new side a real boost ahead of the second half.
The momentum swung the way of the Blades at the end of that opening 45 minutes, and Wilder will be keen for his side to maintain that after the break.

A win could prove absolutely vital for his team, and with West Ham missing some key players, this is surely a big opportunity for the Premier League's bottom club to pick up a much-needed three points.
McBurnie comes on for Osula at the break.
Will that give the Blades a boost in attack?
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Brereton is the 10th Chilean player to score a Premier League goal, and the first since Alexis Sanchez for Manchester United against Newcastle United in October 2018.

McBurnie has scored in each of his last three home Premier League appearances for Sheffield United, a club record for consecutive scoring appearances at Bramall Lane in the competition, but has ended on the losing side in all three games.
He’s the only player in Premier League history to achieve this unfortunate feat for any club.
Can he net again here, and this time with a better result?
A short corner ends with Hamer crossing into the West Ham box, but Trusty's header goalwards is poor and flies high and wide of the target.
It's been a decent start to the half for the hosts, though.
West Ham have won their last three Premier League games against Sheffield United, keeping a clean sheet each time.
They had only won two of their previous 12 league meetings with the Blades before this (six draws, four losses).
A Hamer free-kick ends up with McBurnie at the back post, but after his initial header is blocked, he then loops the rebound over the crossbar.
The Blades are on top at the moment.
WHAT A MISS! A golden opportunity for the Blades to take the lead comes and goes as Brereton latches onto McAtee's throughball.
The forward bears down on goal before firing, but he can only drag his shot well wide of the left post! That could prove to be a crucial miss.
The hosts have had 57.8 per cent of the possession so far in this game, as well as 16 shots to West Ham's seven.
However, the score remains level at one apiece.
Moyes must surely be looking to make a change soon, with the hosts growing in momentum.
However, injuries and other availability issues mean his bench is seriously depleted.
The Hammers are struggling to get much going in attack, with the absences of Lucas Paqueta and Kudus looming large.
Which of the visiting players can step up for their team?
Brereton, having equalised near the end of the first half, makes way for Archer as Wilder looks to freshen up his attack.
Brooks goes in the book for scything down the marauding Emerson.
Ward-Prowse's delivery into the box finds the head of Mavropanos, though the centre-back's header is poor and flies into the West Ham fans behind the goal.
Moyes' first substitution sees Johnson come on for Cornet.
Both goalscorers have now made way for their respective teams.
With 18 or so minutes to play at Bramall Lane, can either of these sides find a winner to give a big boost to their respective ambitions?
Ings cuts onto his right foot before lashing goalwards from 25 yards out, though his deflected shot is comfortably saved by Foderingham.
That is the closest the visitors have come for a while.
Ahmedhodzic is cautioned for hauling down Ings as West Ham looked to counter.
Trusty momentarily goes down in pain after a coming-together with Bowen, though the Blades defender will be okay to carry on.
PENALTY TO WEST HAM!!! It's a rash challenge from Hamer that gives the referee a decision to make.
Ings powers into the box, and having just nipped the ball away from Hamer, the Blades midfielder brings him down, with the referee pointing straight to the spot.
What a chance for the visitors to retake the lead!

GOOOAAALLL!!! WARD-PROWSE MAKES NO MISTAKE FROM THE SPOT!!! The midfielder is so reliable in dead-ball situations, and he fires his penalty straight down the middle and into the back of the net with Foderingham guessing wrong.
2-1 to the Hammers!
In response to his team falling behind for a second time, Wilder brings on Norrington-Davies for Trusty.
Brewster also enters the fray, on in place of Brooks.
Sheffield United have now conceded 17 goals in the last 15 minutes of the second half, more than any other team in the Premier League this season.
That has been one of the many problems the Blades have experienced this term.
The hosts have to respond again here.
They have been the better side, but their lack of quality in attack has once again let them down.
Bowen misses a great opportunity to potentially kill the game off as he curls towards the top corner on his left foot.
He just cannot get quite enough bend on his effort, and the ball flies past the left post.
Of Ward-Prowse's 53 Premier League goals, 31 have either been direct free-kicks (17) or penalties (14).
He is the only player to score 50+ Premier League goals and have at least half of them come via direct free-kicks or penalties (58.5 per cent)
Wilder brings on Norwood for Vinicius as he tries to desperately find a way back into the game for his team.
The fourth official puts up his board and indicates there will be six minutes of additional time at the end of this game.
Can the Blades find another leveller?
Brewster is booked for a crunching challenge on Emerson, one that causes a brief fracas between the two sets of players.
However, the VAR is taking a look, and there may be further punishment coming here for the substitute...
BREWSTER IS SENT OFF!!! The VAR takes a look, and after sending the referee to the pitchside monitor, Brewster receives his marching orders.
It was a very late and needless challenge, and the substitute is sent for an early bath.
Coufal is booked, meanwhile, for his role in the melee following Brewster's poor challenge.
Ings has a couple of bites at the cherry as West Ham look to kill the game off, though his efforts are blocked.
The visitors still have the ball, however, just moments away from a big three points on the road.
While he doesn't come away with a goal, Ings has put in a real shift here and had a hand in both West Ham goals.
He makes way for Mubama as the seconds continue to tick away.
WEST HAM ARE DOWN TO 10 MEN!!! Just moments after picking up his first booking, Coufal is now given his marching orders too with both sides now down to 10! His second is for a challenge on McAtee.

PENALTY TO SHEFFIELD UNITED!!! What a huge decision from the referee, who having seen Areola take out McBurnie as the pair competed to reach a cross, decides to point to the spot! Incredible late drama at Bramall Lane!!! Can the hosts take advantage?
The tension is continuing to build with Areola, who just gave the penalty away, down on the turf.
This must be absolutely agonising for everybody inside Bramall Lane, nobody more so than McAtee, who is stood with the ball in his hands waiting to take the spot-kick!
Areola is forced off, with Fabianski on to try and save the penalty and secure the three points for his side! Can he save his team-mate after his crucial error?
GOOOAAALLL!!! MCBURNIE SCORES FROM THE SPOT TO LEVEL!!! While McAtee was stood with the ball in his hands, it was simply a tactic to take the pressure off McBurnie.
The striker is the man instead trusted to take the penalty, and he repays that faith by rifling into the bottom-left corner to make it 2-2!!!
PENALTY!?!? It's West Ham's turn to ask for a late spot-kick, as Ahmedhodzic and Bowen clash in the box.
The referee instead points for a Sheffield United free-kick, and that might be that...
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-2 WEST HAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring to an end a pulsating 2-2 draw at Bramall Lane, with Sheffield United and West Ham forced to share the spoils.
Cornet put the visitors into the lead on his first Premier League start of the season, pouncing upon a loose ball to lash home.
The hosts responded, however, with Brereton latching onto a rebound before rifling into the back of the net to level on the stroke of half-time.
West Ham's lead was restored with 11 minutes to play, Hamer bringing down Ings in the penalty area before the ever-reliable Ward-Prowse made no mistake from the spot.
It looked like the Hammers were on their way to three points when Brewster was given a straight red for a needless challenge on Emerson in added time.
But after Coufal received two bookings in quick succession to also be given his marching orders, Areola came for a cross and failed to get there, instead clearing out McBurnie.
The referee pointed to the spot, and after McBurnie picked himself up off the turf, the striker drilled home his penalty to secure a point for his side.
The draw is not enough to move the Blades off the bottom, though they do close the gap on safety to seven points.
For the Hammers, the late disappointment means they miss the opportunity to close the gap on Tottenham to three points.
It's Bournemouth at home in the Premier League up next for West Ham, while Sheffield United will host Brighton in the FA Cup fourth round next weekend.
That is all we have for you from Bramall Lane, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
